title: Blind Source Separation (Special Topics in Communication Engineering)
objectives:
Introduce the framework of well-known Blind Source Separation (BSS) problems and
apply them to various scenarios in fields like telecommunication systems, biomedical
engineering, and control.
Familiarize students with the main scenarios mentioned and appropriate methods for
solving problems within these scenarios.
By the end of the course, students will be familiar with real-world applications of BSS
in fields like telecommunication and biomedical engineering. They will model
problems as mixtures of sources and answer posed questions.
Students will study BSS models in telecommunications, focusing on radio and audio
signals.
Students will study BSS models in biomedical data, including images and brain
signals.
Students will extract suitable features from data, categorize the data, and apply them
in machine learning approaches.
syllabus:
Introduction to Blind Source Separation and its practical applications (3 sessions)
Linear BSS models (4 sessions)
Nonlinear BSS models (3 sessions)
Structured linear BSS models (4 sessions)
Sparse BSS models (3 sessions)
BSS in underdetermined systems (4 sessions)
Multi-way BSS models (2 sessions)
Similarity measures in BSS (2 sessions)
BSS in spatio-temporal mixtures (2 sessions)
textbooks:
1. P. Comon, C. Jutten, Blind Source Separation: Independent component analysis and
applications, Academic Press, 2010.
2. Almeida, Luis B., Nonlinear source separation, Springer Nature, 2022.
3. Naik, Ganesh R., and Wenwu Wang, Blind source separation, Springer, 2014.
